facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lived in Mongolia and China during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus (meaning "plank lizard") is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in what is now Mongolia and China during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago).

facts.statement: The type species Pinacosaurus grangeri was named in 1933 based on fossils discovered in 1923.
facts.quote: The genus contains two species; the type species, Pinacosaurus grangeri, was named in 1933 based on fossils found in 1923.

facts.statement: A second species, Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum, was named in 2026.
facts.quote: A second species, Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum, was named in 2026.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaurine measuring about 5 meters in length and weighing up to 1.9 metric tons.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaurine, about 5 m long and weighed up to 1.9 MT.

facts.statement: The head of Pinacosaurus was protected by bone tiles, which inspired the genus name meaning "plank lizard".
facts.quote: The head was protected by bone tiles, hence its name.

facts.statement: The neck, back, and tail of Pinacosaurus were protected by armor made of keeled osteoderms.
facts.quote: Neck, back and tail were protected by an armour of keeled osteoderms.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus could actively defend itself using a tail club.
facts.quote: The animal could also actively defend itself by means of a tail club.

facts.statement: The American Museum of Natural History sponsored Central Asiatic Expeditions to the Gobi Desert in Mongolia during the 1920s.
facts.quote: The American Museum of Natural History sponsored several Central Asiatic Expeditions to the Gobi Desert in Mongolia in the 1920s.

facts.statement: The original specimens of Pinacosaurus were found by Walter W. Granger in 1923 at the "Flaming Cliffs" of the Djadokhta Formation in Shabarakh Usu.
facts.quote: Among the many paleontological finds from the "Flaming Cliffs" of the Djadokhta Formation in Shabarakh Usu (Bayn Dzak) were the original specimens of Pinacosaurus, found by Walter W. Granger in 1923.

facts.statement: The generic name Pinacosaurus is derived from the Greek word for "plank," referring to the small rectangular scutes on its head.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek πίναξ, pinax, "plank", in reference to the small rectangular scutes covering the head.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 6523 was found in the Campanian-aged Djadokhta Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, AMNH 6523, was found in a layer of the Djadokhta Formation, dating from the Campanian.

facts.statement: The holotype skull remains the largest known skull of the genus Pinacosaurus.
facts.quote: The skull is still the largest known of the genus.

facts.statement: In 1923, H. C. T'an and Otto Zdansky collected remains from the Wangshi Group in Shandong, China, which were later described as Pinacosaurus cf. grangeri by Buffetaut in 1995.
facts.quote: In 1923, a well-preserved sacrum with the attached right ilium and part of the presacral rod, caudal vertebrae, a left femur and a dermal scute was collected from the Wangshi Group in Shandong, China by H. C. T'an and Otto Zdansky and was described as Pinacosaurus cf. grangeri by Buffetaut (1995).

facts.statement: Soviet-Mongolian expeditions in 1969 and 1970 reported finding thirty Pinacosaurus skeletons.
facts.quote: Soviet-Mongolian expeditions in 1969 and 1970 reported thirty skeletons.

facts.statement: Mongolian-Japanese expeditions between 1993 and 1998 added another thirty Pinacosaurus skeletons to the known record.
facts.quote: Mongolian-Japanese expeditions added another thirty between 1993 and 1998.

facts.statement: Canadian expeditions between 2001 and 2006 reported finding forty Pinacosaurus skeletons.
facts.quote: Forty were reported by Canadian expeditions between 2001 and 2006.

facts.statement: Unlike many ankylosaurs preserved on their backs, most Pinacosaurus juveniles are found on their bellies in a resting position with legs tucked in.
facts.quote: Whereas ankylosaur skeletons have often been preserved laying on their back, most Pinacosaurus juveniles are found on their belly in a resting position, with the legs tucked in.

facts.statement: Undescribed material includes finds of several juveniles huddled together, likely killed by a sandstorm.
facts.quote: Other, as yet undescribed material included two finds of several juveniles huddled together, evidently killed by a sandstorm.

facts.statement: Teresa Maryańska described a well-preserved juvenile skull in 1971 and 1977.
facts.quote: A well-preserved juvenile skull was described by Teresa Maryańska in 1971 and 1977.

facts.statement: Robert Hill studied the juvenile specimen IGM 100/1014 in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, Robert Hill studied the juvenile specimen IGM 100/1014.

facts.statement: In 2011, Currie published a study on the hands and feet of Pinacosaurus, parts often incompletely known in other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2011, Currie published a study on the hand and foot, body parts often incompletely known with other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: In 2011, the postcranial skeleton MPC 100/1305 was described in detail, though it was initially referred to Saichania.
facts.quote: Also in 2011, the postcranial skeleton MPC 100/1305 was described in detail, though at the time referred to Saichania.

facts.statement: Yang Zhongjian described the species Pinacosaurus ninghsiensis in 1935 based on a specimen from the Bayan Mandahu Formation in Ningxia Province.
facts.quote: Yang Zhongjian ("C. C. Young") discovered a new specimen in the Ningxia Province at the Bayan Mandahu Formation, and described it as a new species Pinacosaurus ninghsiensis in 1935.

facts.statement: Fragmentary remains known as specimen PIN 614, originally described as Syrmosaurus viminocaudus by Maleev in 1952, are now considered the same species as P. grangeri.
facts.quote: The same is true of fragmentary remains, specimen PIN 614, described as Syrmosaurus viminocaudus by Evgenii Aleksandrovich Maleev in 1952.

facts.statement: Heishansaurus pachycephalus was first described in 1953 as a pachycephalosaur and was often considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: It was first described in 1953 as a pachycephalosaur and had been usually considered a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: A Belgian-Chinese expedition discovered a large articulated skeleton in the Bayan Mandahu Formation in 1996.
facts.quote: In 1996, a Belgian-Chinese expedition discovered a large and articulated skeleton in the Bayan Mandahu Formation.

facts.statement: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named the species Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus in 1999, with holotype specimen IMM 96BM3/1.
facts.quote: It was named as Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus, holotype specimen IMM 96BM3/1, by Pascal Godefroit et al. in 1999.

facts.statement: The specific name P. mephistocephalus combines "Mephistopheles" and the Greek word for "head," referencing the "devilish" squamosal horns.
facts.quote: The specific name is a contraction of Mephistopheles and Greek κεφαλή, kephalè, "head", in reference to the "devilish" squamosal horns.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul suggested that P. mephistocephalus was a junior synonym of P. grangeri.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul suggested that P. mephistocephalus were a junior synonym of P. grangeri.

facts.statement: Robert Hill considered P. mephistocephalus a valid species in 2012 based on its secondary dermal horns and narial characteristics.
facts.quote: It was considered a valid species by Robert Hill in 2012, based on the "secondary dermal" (squamosal) horns and narial characteristics.

facts.statement: In 2026, Paul Penkalski transferred P. mephistocephalus to the genus Eopinacosaurus based on differences in the skull and cranial osteoderms.
facts.quote: In 2026, Paul Penkalski transferred P. mephistocephalus to its own genus, Eopinacosaurus, based on various differences in the skull and cranial osteoderms.

facts.statement: In 1995, Eric Buffetaut referred ankylosaurian remains from Shandong to the genus Pinacosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1995, Eric Buffetaut referred ankylosaurian remains found in Shandong to a Pinacosaurus sp.

facts.statement: Synonyms for Pinacosaurus include Pinacosaurus ninghsiensis, Heishansaurus pachycephalus, and Syrmosaurus viminocaudus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Pinacosaurus ninghsiensis Young, 1935 Heishansaurus pachycephalus? Bohlin, 1953 Syrmosaurus viminocaudus Maleev, 1952

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum is a subdivision of the genus Pinacosaurus.
facts.quote: subdivision: †Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum Penkalski, 2026

facts.statement: In 2015, Arbour and Currie concluded that Heishansaurus pachycephalus was a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2015, Arbour and Currie again concluded it was a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Robert Hill argued in 2012 that P. mephistocephalus was a valid species based on its secondary dermal horns and narial characteristics.
facts.quote: It was considered a valid species by Robert Hill in 2012, based on the "secondary dermal" (squamosal) horns and narial characteristics.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was a lightly built, medium-sized animal that reached a total length of 5 meters when fully grown.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus was a lightly built, medium-sized animal, fully grown individuals reached a total length of 5 m.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the body mass of Pinacosaurus at 1.9 tonnes, while Thomas R. Holtz estimated it to be similar to that of a horse.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated its body mass at 1.9 t, while Thomas R. Holtz estimated it to have a body mass of a horse.

facts.statement: The upper snout armor of Pinacosaurus consists of a fused mass rather than distinct tiles or caputegulae.
facts.quote: The upper snout armour does not consist of distinct tiles, caputegulae, but of a fused mass.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus grangeri has a notch in the snout armor just above the innermost nostril opening.
facts.quote: P. grangeri has a notch in the snout armour just above the innermost nostril opening.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus has squamosal horns that extend beyond the rear of the skull roof, with their points marking the widest part of the skull rather than the eye sockets.
facts.quote: P. mephistocephalus has squamosal horns extending to behind beyond the rear of the skull roof, their points representing the widest point of the skull, instead of the upper rims of the eye sockets.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Pinacosaurus bears about fourteen teeth.
facts.quote: The maxilla bears about fourteen teeth.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus has at least three oval holes in the narial vestibule on each side of the skull.
facts.quote: With Pinacosaurus there are at least three per side.

facts.statement: In juvenile Pinacosaurus, the C hole consists of secondary smaller openings; Godefroit et al. described four pairs in 1999 and a later specimen had five pairs in 2003.
facts.quote: In Pinacosaurus juveniles the C hole seems to consist of secondary smaller openings of varying number: Godefroit et al. described four pairs of openings in total in 1999, and in 2003 a juvenile specimen with five pairs of openings was described.

facts.statement: The precise function of the multiple nostril openings in Pinacosaurus is unclear.
facts.quote: The precise function of this arrangement is unclear.

facts.statement: A 2015 description of a juvenile Pinacosaurus revealed a complex hyoid bone apparatus.
facts.quote: In 2015, a juvenile specimen was described showing a complex hyoid bone or tongue bone apparatus.

facts.statement: The strong development of the hyoid bone in Pinacosaurus suggests a powerful tongue compensated for weakly developed teeth.
facts.quote: The strong development of the hyoid would indicate that a powerful tongue compensated for the weakly developed dentition.

facts.statement: Some bones from the Pinacosaurus hyoid apparatus specimen were later reinterpreted as part of the larynx.
facts.quote: However, some of these bones from the specimen were later reinterpreted as the larynx.

facts.statement: Most known Pinacosaurus fossils are juveniles, but the P. mephistocephalus holotype (IMM 96BM3/1) is no longer than about 3 meters.
facts.quote: Most of these represent juveniles; however, even specimen IMM 96BM3/1, the P. mephistocephalus holotype, is no longer than about 3 m.

facts.statement: The hand of Pinacosaurus is completely known, an exceptional state for ankylosaurids, with a phalangeal formula of 2-3-3-3-2.
facts.quote: The hand is completely known, which is exceptional for ankylosaurids. It has five digits, and the phalangeal formula is 2-3-3-3-2, meaning that the innermost finger of the forelimb has two bones, the next has three, etc.

facts.statement: The claws of Pinacosaurus are hoof-shaped.
facts.quote: The claws are hoof-shaped.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus has three toes on its foot, correcting Maryańska's 1977 assumption of four toes which was based on a damaged specimen.
facts.quote: The foot has three toes, not four as Maryańska assumed in 1977, misled by the damaged specimen ZPAL MgD−II/9.

facts.statement: The sides of the rump and tail of Pinacosaurus were covered with moderately long, flat, recurved, triangular spikes.
facts.quote: The sides of the rump and the tail were occupied by moderately long, flat, recurved, triangular spikes.

facts.statement: Originally classified in Nodosauridae by Gilmore, Pinacosaurus is now considered an ankylosaurid and likely a member of the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Originally placed in the Nodosauridae by Gilmore, Pinacosaurus is now considered to be an ankylosaurid and a likely member of the Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: Juvenile Pinacosaurus possessed large tongue bones showing signs of muscular stress, suggesting they relied heavily on muscular tongues for feeding.
facts.quote: A juvenile specimen of Pinacosaurus preserves large paraglossalia (triangular bones or cartilages located in the tongue) which show signs of muscular stress

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus likely had a varied diet that included tough leaves and pulpy fruits, though it probably avoided fibrous and woody plants.
facts.quote: Though Pinacosaurus may not have fed on fibrous and woody plants, they may have had a more varied diet, including tough leaves and pulpy fruits

facts.statement: The structure of Pinacosaurus's tongue and teeth might suggest it exhibited ant-eater-like insectivorous behavior.
facts.quote: Inversely, this might suggest ant-eater-like insectivorous behaviour

facts.statement: A group of juvenile Pinacosaurus found at Bayan Mandahu were all oriented in the same direction, suggesting they were a traveling herd killed and buried by a sandstorm.
facts.quote: In the group of juveniles found together at Bayan Mandahu, the individuals were all oriented into the same direction, suggesting they represent a travelling true herd simultaneously killed and covered by a sandstorm

facts.statement: Juvenile Pinacosaurus found in groups were all approximately the same age, with an average length of about 1.5 meters.
facts.quote: It is remarkable that the members of such groups are all of about the same age, having an average length of circa 1.5 metres

facts.statement: During growth, juvenile Pinacosaurus developed fused ribs and increasingly robust forelimbs, indicating that their arms bore most of their body weight.
facts.quote: During their ontogenetic development, in juveniles at first the ribs fused with their vertebrae. The forelimbs strongly increased in robustness, while the hindlimbs did not become larger relative to the rest of the skeleton, indicating that the arms bore most of the weight

facts.statement: A fossilized larynx was described from a juvenile Pinacosaurus specimen by Yoshida et al. in 2023.
facts.quote: A fossilized larynx was described from a specimen of juvenile P. hilwitnorum (IGM 100/3186) by Yoshida et al. 2023

facts.statement: The structure of the Pinacosaurus larynx suggests it was capable of making loud, possibly bird-like vocalizations.
facts.quote: This structure suggests that Pinacosaurus was likely capable of making loud, possibly bird-like vocalizations

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lived in a semi-desert habitat interspersed with oases.
facts.quote: The habitat of Pinacosaurus consisted of a semi-desert interspersed with oases

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Pinacosaurus had a relatively light build to gain agility for fighting small theropods, using its club to hit swift targets.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that the relatively light build of Pinacosaurus was an adaptation to gain agility to better fight small theropods, the moderately large club being fast enough to hit these swift targets

facts.statement: The genus Pinacosaurus was named by Gilmore in 1933.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Gilmore, 1933

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Pinacosaurus is Pinacosaurus grangeri.
facts.quote: type_species: Pinacosaurus grangeri

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus is a subdivision of the genus described by Godefroit et al. in 1999.
facts.quote: subdivision: Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus Godefroit et al. 1999

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus has between two and five additional openings near the nostrils, the purpose of which remains unexplained.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus tiene entre dos y 5 orificios adicionales junto a las narinas, que todavía no han sido explicados

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaur, about five meters long and weighing up to two tons.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus era una anquilosaurio de tamaño mediano, de unos cinco metros de largo y que pesaba hasta dos toneladas

facts.statement: The head of Pinacosaurus was protected by bone scales, which is the origin of its name.
facts.quote: La cabeza estaba protegida por tejas de hueso, de ahí su nombre

facts.statement: The neck, back, and tail of Pinacosaurus were protected by an armor of osteoderms with a keel.
facts.quote: El cuello, la espalda y la cola estaban protegidos por una armadura de osteodermos con quilla

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus could actively defend itself using a club-like tail.
facts.quote: El animal también podría defenderse activamente mediante un garrote de cola

facts.statement: Like other ankylosaurs, Pinacosaurus had a thick club at the end of its tail used as a defensive weapon against large predators.
facts.quote: Como todos los anquilosáuridos, tenía una gruesa maza en el extremo final de su cola que utilizaba como arma defensiva contra grandes depredadores

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Pinacosaurus weight at around 1.9 tons, while Thomas R. Holtz estimated it between 454 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimó su peso alrededor de 1,9 toneladas, sin embargo Thomas R. Holtz lo estimó entre 454 y 907 kilogramos

facts.statement: The PIN 614 postcranial skeleton of Pinacosaurus measures 3.66 meters from the first neck vertebra to the end of the tail.
facts.quote: El PIN 614 esqueleto postcraneal mide 3,66 metros desde la primera vértebra del cuello hasta el final de la cola

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus had a short, thick skull that curved downward to form a toothless parrot-like beak.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus poseían un cráneo corto y grueso que se curvaba hacia abajo hasta formar un pico de loro sin dientes

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus had rows of small, weak teeth inside its mouth that influenced its diet.
facts.quote: En el interior de la boca tenían hileras de dientes pequeños y débiles que condicionaban su dieta

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus likely avoided hard stems and pine needles, instead ingesting soft, low-growing ferns that were easy to cut.
facts.quote: Probablemente evitaban los tallos duros y las agujas de pino y en cambio ingería los blandos y bajos helechos, fáciles de desbrozar

facts.statement: Inside the snout of Pinacosaurus, numerous curved and thin bones run together to form an S-shape.
facts.quote: En el interior del hocico se presentan multitud de huesos curvos y finos que en conjunto discurren formando una S

facts.statement: Godefroit et al. described four additional nasal openings in 1999, and a juvenile specimen with five openings was described in 2003.
facts.quote: Godefroit et al. describieron cuatro en 1999, y en 2003 un espécimen juvenil fue descrito con cinco aberturas

facts.statement: In 2014, Arbour established some distinctive traits of the genus Pinacosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2014, Arbor estableció algunos rasgos distintivos del género.

facts.statement: The upper snout armor of Pinacosaurus consists of a fused mass rather than distinct scales called caputegulae.
facts.quote: La armadura del hocico superior no consta de baldosas distintas, caputegula, sino de una masa fusionada.

facts.statement: Adult individuals of Pinacosaurus have a skull that is longer than it is wide.
facts.quote: Los individuos adultos tienen un cráneo que es más largo que ancho.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus differs from Crichtonpelta by lacking an ornamented posterior edge on the skull roof and having cheek horns that do not curve upward.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus se diferencia de Crichtonpelta en la falta de un borde posterior adornado del techo del cráneo y en que el cuerno de la mejilla no se curva hacia arriba.

facts.statement: Known adult skulls of Pinacosaurus have a length of about 30 centimeters.
facts.quote: Los cráneos adultos conocidos tienen una longitud de unos 30 centímetros.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Pinacosaurus has about 14 teeth.
facts.quote: El maxilar tiene unos 14 dientes.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus has at least three oval holes per side within its large nasal vestibule.
facts.quote: Con Pinacosaurus hay al menos tres por lado.

facts.statement: Godefroit et al. described a total of 4 pairs of openings in 1999, and a juvenile specimen with 5 pairs of openings was described in 2003.
facts.quote: Godefroit et al. describió 4 pares de aberturas en total en 1999, y en 2003 se describió un ejemplar juvenil con 5 pares de aberturas.

facts.statement: The dermal scale horn does not cover the entire squamosal bone, creating the illusion of an additional skull bone in front of the horn.
facts.quote: El cuerno escamoso no cubre todo el escamoso, creando la ilusión de que hay un hueso de cráneo adicional frente al cuerno.

facts.statement: A distinctive feature is that the quadratojugal touches the postorbital, whereas in other Thyreophora where this condition is known, these bones are separated by the jugal.
facts.quote: Un rasgo distintivo real es que el cuadratoyugal toca el postorbital, mientras que en otros Thyreophora para los que se conoce la afección, estos huesos están separados por el yugal.

facts.statement: In 2015, a juvenile specimen was described showing a complex hyoid or tongue bone apparatus.
facts.quote: En 2015, se describió un espécimen juvenil que mostraba un complejo aparato de hueso hioides o de lengua.

facts.statement: Most known postcranial skeletons represent juveniles, and even the holotype of P. mephistocephalus does not measure more than 3 meters.
facts.quote: La mayoría de estos representan juveniles, incluso el espécimen IMM 96BM3/1, el holotipo de P. mephistocephalus, no mide más de 3 metros.

facts.statement: Like all ankylosaurs, Pinacosaurus had a bony club at the end of its tail that was likely used as a defensive weapon against predators.
facts.quote: Como todos los anquilosaurios, Pinacosaurus tenía un garrote huesudo al final de la cola que probablemente usaba como arma defensiva contra los depredadores.

facts.statement: This tail club was relatively small.
facts.quote: Esta porra era relativamente pequeña.

facts.statement: The forefoot has five digits with a phalangeal formula of 2-3-3-3-2, meaning the innermost digit has two bones and the next has three.
facts.quote: Tiene cinco dígitos y la fórmula de la falange es 2-3-3-3-2, lo que significa que el dedo más interno de la extremidad anterior tiene dos huesos, el siguiente tiene tres.

facts.statement: As in all known ankylosaurs, the foot has three toes, not four as Maryańska assumed in 1977, misled by the damaged specimen ZPAL MgD-II/9.
facts.quote: Como en todos los anquilosáuridos conocidos, el pie tiene tres dedos, no cuatro como supuso Maryańska en 1977, engañado por el espécimen dañado ZPAL MgD-II/9.

facts.statement: The neck is protected by two cervical semirings consisting of rectangular segments with a keel fused to an underlying bone band.
facts.quote: El cuello está protegido por dos semianillos cervicales, que consisten en segmentos rectangulares con quilla fusionados a una banda ósea subyacente.

facts.statement: This bone band is completely ossified even in juvenile individuals.
facts.quote: Esta banda está completamente osificada incluso en individuos juveniles.

facts.statement: The sides of the rump and tail were occupied by triangular, flat, recurved, and moderately long spines.
facts.quote: Los lados de la rabadilla y la cola estaban ocupados por púas triangulares, planas, recurvadas y moderadamente largas.

facts.statement: On the back were present parallel rows of smaller keeled oval osteoderms.
facts.quote: En el dorso estaban presentes filas paralelas de osteodermos de quilla ovalada más pequeños.

facts.statement: There is no continuous "sacral shield" on the hip made of fused plates.
facts.quote: No hay un "escudo sacro" continuo en la cadera, hecho de placas fusionadas.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus belongs to the parent group Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosaurinae

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus is classified in the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lived from the Coniacian to the Campanian stages, between 89.8 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Campanian (89.8 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The precise function of the nasal opening arrangement is not clear.
facts.quote: La función precisa de esta disposición no está clara.

facts.statement: It has been suggested that some additional holes are the result of damage.
facts.quote: también se ha sugerido que algunos orificios adicionales son el resultado de daños.

facts.statement: Maryańska in 1977 thought the structure was a tabular bone unknown in dinosaurs, suggesting Ankylosauria evolved independently of Aetosauria, a hypothesis now completely discarded.
facts.quote: Maryańska en 1977 pensó que se trataba de un hueso tabular, por lo demás desconocido en los dinosaurios, lo que demuestra que la Ankylosauria había evolucionado independientemente de la Aetosauria, una hipótesis hoy totalmente descartada.

facts.statement: The strong development of the hyoid suggests that a powerful tongue compensated for weakly developed dentition.
facts.quote: El fuerte desarrollo del hioides indicaría que una lengua poderosa compensaba la dentición débilmente desarrollada.

facts.statement: It was inferred that all dinosaurs had such complex tongue bones, but these generally disappeared during fossilization.
facts.quote: Se infirió que todos los dinosaurios tenían huesos de la lengua tan complejos, pero que estos generalmente se perdían durante la fosilización.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus differs from distant relatives Gobisaurus and Shamosaurus by having additional openings in the nasal fossa and a pointed caputegula protruding from the prefrontal directed forward.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus difiere de aquellos en posesión de aberturas adicionales en la fosa nasal y una caputegula puntiaguda que sobresale en el prefrontal, dirigida hacia el frente.

facts.statement: P. grangeri has a notch in the snout armor just above the opening of the most internal nostril.
facts.quote: P. grangeri tiene una muesca en la armadura del hocico justo encima de la abertura de la nariz más interna.

facts.statement: P. mephistocephalus has dermal horns that extend backward beyond the rear of the skull roof, and their tips represent the widest point of the skull, rather than the upper edges of the eye sockets.
facts.quote: P. mephistocephalus tiene cuernos escamosos que se extienden hacia atrás más allá de la parte posterior del techo del cráneo, y sus puntas representan el punto más ancho del cráneo, en lugar de los bordes superiores de las cuencas de los ojos.

facts.statement: P. mephistocephalus also has a clear transverse narrowing of the skull roof at the level of the lacrimals, just in front of the eye sockets.
facts.quote: P. mephistocephalus también tiene un estrechamiento transversal claro del techo del cráneo al nivel de los lagrimales, justo en frente de las cuencas de los ojos.

facts.statement: Visible sutures of skull elements in juvenile specimens allowed for the first time to determine their precise arrangement.
facts.quote: Las suturas visibles de los elementos del cráneo en ejemplares juveniles permitieron por primera vez determinar su disposición precisa.

facts.statement: Various skull openings such as the antorbital fenestra and temporal fenestra apparently closed at a very young age because they are no longer visible even in found juveniles.
facts.quote: Varias aberturas del cráneo como la fenestra antorbitaria y la fenestra temporal aparentemente se cerraron a una edad muy temprana porque ya no son visibles incluso en los juveniles encontrados.

facts.statement: The torso is very flat.
facts.quote: El torso es muy plano.

facts.statement: The forelimbs are moderately robust; the holotype of P. mephistocephalus has a fairly robust humerus and ulna, however, the hand is completely known, which is exceptional for ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores son moderadamente robustas, el holotipo de P. mephistocephalus tiene un húmero y el cúbito bastante robusto, sin embargo, la mano es completamente conocida, lo que es excepcional para los anquilosaurios.

facts.statement: The metatarsals are tightly packed and remain vertical.
facts.quote: Los metatarsianos están estrechamente apretados y se mantienen verticales.

facts.statement: In the pelvis, the iliac bones widen strongly outward toward the front.

facts.statement: The ischium is thin and curves forward.

facts.statement: The hind legs are moderately robust.
facts.quote: Las patas traseras son moderadamente robustas.

facts.statement: The tibia has a wide lower part with well-formed condyles.
facts.quote: La tibia tiene una parte inferior ancha con cóndilos bien formados.

facts.statement: Currie assumed that the lower leg articulated directly with the metatarsus, the inner part of the astragalus and the entire calcaneus were absent, or there were no ossified cartilage elements.
facts.quote: Currie asumió que la parte inferior de la pierna se articulaba directamente con el metatarso, la parte interna del astrágalo y todo el calcáneo estaban ausentes o no había elementos de cartílago osificados.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula of the foot digits is variable; most individuals have 0-3-3-4-0, but some specimens possess an additional penultimate phalanx on the third digit resulting in 0-3-4-4-0, while others lack a phalanx on the fourth foot digit, resulting in a 0-3-3-3-0 configuration.
facts.quote: La fórmula de la falange de los dedos de los pies es variable, la mayoría de los individuos tienen 0−3−3−4−0 pero algunos ejemplares poseen una penúltima falange adicional en el tercer dedo, lo que resulta en 0-3-4-4-0, mientras que otros carecen de una falange en el cuarto dedo del pie, lo que provoca una configuración 0-3-3-3-0.

facts.statement: Godefroit assumed Pinacosaurus differed from other species by having three or four segments instead of the usual six, but Arbour concluded that the normal number was present.
facts.quote: Godefroit asumió Pinacosaurus se diferenciaba de otras especies en tener tres o cuatro segmentos en lugar de los seis habituales, pero Arbour concluyó que el número normal estaba presente.
